thread:
oncall-bot: [P1] Serving runtime alerts — model warmup failures on prod-serving-pool-3 (nyc). ~40% of warmup tasks failing for model gpt-open-13b-qlora-v2. Paging @alex @priya. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/warmup-failures

alex: I’m on it. Pulling kube + pod logs for pool-3. Priorities: 1) limit customer impact (route new requests to fallbacks), 2) stop canary rollout if that’s the trigger, 3) investigate node crash/OOM patterns.

priya: quick glance — two distinct errors in logs: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while initializing weights` and `deserialize: unexpected EOF while reading shard` across different pods. Also seeing `nvrtc: compilation timed out` on one node.

sam: pod on node-43 got OOMKilled during model init. log snippet from pod prod/pool-3/gpt-load-43:
```
[init] loading shard 0/4
loading weights...
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while initializing weights (requested 2.1 GiB)
[retries] attempt 1 failed, retrying warmup
deserialize: unexpected EOF (shard size mismatch)
[container] process exited with code 137 (OOMKilled)
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollout metadata: gpt-open-13b-qlora-v2 -> prod-serving-pool-3 started 5m ago by ci/cd pipeline #build-9842. Suggest immediate rollback of canary.

alex: rolling back canary now. Also enabling traffic-shed rule to route new generation requests away from pool-3 to fallback route (gpt-open-7b-qlora) until we stabilize. Notifying CS.

miguel: spinning up 3 extra nodes in pool-3 to give scheduler headroom and prevent cold-start OOM cascades. Also kicking a rolling restart to clear bad caches.

jane-cs: pinging the impacted customers (dedicated clients on dedicated-pool-3 and a small subset of hosted tenants). Template: "We're seeing transient model warmup failures impacting some requests; we've rolled back the canary and are routing traffic to fallback models; we'll update within 30m."

priya: digging into the deserialization EOF — could be a corrupted checkpoint shard pushed by the model onboarding job. Checking artifact store checksums vs. nodes. If shard mismatches, nodes will repeatedly OOM at load.

sam: also observed one node with nvrtc compile timeout:
```
[compile] nvrtc: compilation timed out after 120s for kernel select_ccs.cu
[info] falling back to interpreter path, slower inference but avoids compile hang
```
This explains some long stalls and retry spikes.

alex: mitigation summary so far: 1) canary rolled back, 2) traffic routed to fallback 7B model, 3) extra nodes added to pool, 4) rolling restart started, 5) CS notified. Early metric: error rate on pool-3 warmups down from 37% -> 6% after rollback and routing.

priya: Checksum check results: two shards for v2 have mismatching checksums in the artifact bucket (shard-1, shard-3). That matches the pods that keep failing on deserialization. Looks like an incomplete push during model onboarding.

miguel: isolating corrupted artifacts by blacklisting the artifact paths impacted and forcing nodes to re-pull from the last-good commit. Kicking a job to re-sync shards from backup.

sam: for the NVRTC timeouts — bypass compile by setting ENV FORCE_INTERPRETER=1 for warmup jobs temporarily. This reduces the chance of compile-time hangs while we debug kernel issues.

alex: making call: keep rollout rolled back, blacklist corrupted shards, re-sync artifacts, keep traffic routed to 7B fallback until we've validated a clean v2 artifact. Labeling incident P1 due to customer impact on a few dedicated tenants.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed at +7m. Canary disabled.

priya: after re-sync of shards and re-deploy of a clean artifact to a staging node, warmup succeeded on staging. Will schedule a controlled re-rollout to Canary with very small traffic and strict warmup health checks.

jane-cs: customers updated with status: "We rolled back the problematic model and rerouted traffic. No data loss. We're working on a rebuild and will provide ETA for re-enable in 2h."

alex: documenting next steps for postmortem: 1) root cause: bad artifact pushed during onboarding -> corrupted shards, 2) improve artifact validation pre-publish (checksums + manifest size), 3) add warmup canary gating (full shard-verify on first warmup node), 4) add auto-fallback policy when warmup error > X% instead of only k8 evictions. Assigning postmortem owners: priya (technical write), jane-cs (customer impact), miguel (infra fixes).

priya: note — also file bug with nvrtc/kernel selection team: compile timeouts on certain GPU drivers/versions appear when combined with new quantization codepath. Workaround is FORCE_INTERPRETER until a patched kernel is available.

sam: metrics after mitigations: warmup failures on prod-serving-pool-3 dropped to ~1.8%, request tail latency normalized. 7B fallback carrying ~11% of QPS for 25m.

alex: handing off to priya for the next 4h window — please monitor artifact re-sync, validate shard checksums, and coordinate canary re-roll if clean. I'll be offline for the next 90m but reachable for escalations. Leave a short handoff note in Zoomcall if needed.

priya: ack — will take over. Handoff notes: commands to validate shards: `sha256sum shard-* | sort`, artifact path: s3://models/redwood/gpt-open-13b-qlora-v2/, warmup logs: /var/log/serving/pool-3/*. Also watch for `deserialize: unexpected EOF` or `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory` during init.

oncall-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged, assigned owner: priya. Incident thread will be auto-archived after resolution.

alex: leaving one final note for the postmortem: consider adding a small unit test in CI that attempts a warmup on a tiny dummy node after onboarding artifacts are published (cheap early detection).

priya: sounds good. I'll start the postmortem draft and include action items, timelines, and who to contact for follow-ups.

oncall-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 1812350100 (mitigations applied, fallback in place, postmortem assigned)."
